constraints.name: Two held or active allocations for the same resource must never overlap.
constraints.note: MySQL has no exclusion constraint, so the guarantee moves from the database schema to BookingService: GET_LOCK per module and day, then an overlap re-check and the insert inside one InnoDB transaction. This mirrors the engine's lock_day().

evidence.note: Class comment states the replacement for the exclusion constraint.
The engine's exclusion constraint booking_allocations_no_overlap, the rule being ported.
The engine already serialises bookings per day; the plugin uses the same unit.

constraints.verification: A test that fires parallel booking requests for one slot against real MySQL/MariaDB and asserts exactly one succeeds.

constraints.name: Runs on free self-hosted WordPress: PHP 7.4+, WordPress 6.2+, MySQL 5.7 / MariaDB 10.3, no build step, no Composer at runtime, no outside service.
constraints.note: The user chose WordPress only because of free-tier hosting. WordPress.com's free plan cannot run plugins at all.

evidence.note: Section 1, hosting warning and minimum versions.
Plugin header declares Requires PHP 7.4 and Requires at least 6.2; the autoloader needs no Composer.

constraints.verification: Install the plugin zip into a clean local WordPress on MariaDB; lint with PHP 7.4 compatibility before release.

constraints.name: Every CREATE TABLE follows dbDelta's rules: one column per line, two spaces after PRIMARY KEY, KEY not INDEX, no foreign keys.
constraints.note: dbDelta parses the statements to diff schemas on upgrade; a format slip silently skips a column or index.

evidence.note: Header comment records the rule.

constraints.verification: Activate twice on the same database and compare SHOW CREATE TABLE output: the second run must change nothing.

constraints.name: Instants are stored in UTC (*_utc columns); shift and opening times are wall-clock in the site time zone.
constraints.note: Converting at the edges keeps daylight-saving and site time zone changes from moving stored bookings.

evidence.note: Class comment states the storage rule.

constraints.verification: Engine tests with a site time zone that has daylight saving.

constraints.name: Deactivating never deletes data; deleting the plugin drops tables only when the owner ticked the delete-data setting.
constraints.note: Owners on free hosts often delete and reinstall plugins to fix problems; losing every booking that way would be unrecoverable.

evidence.note: Drops tables only when jsb_delete_data_on_uninstall is '1'.
Clears only the cron hook.

constraints.verification: Deactivate, reactivate and check row counts; delete with the setting off and on.

constraints.name: src/Engine holds no WordPress calls, so its rules are unit-tested without WordPress.
constraints.note: Planned boundary from the confirmed plan; it keeps the ported allocation rules testable like the Python originals.

evidence.note: Section 2, plugin layout: src/Engine is pure PHP.

constraints.verification: PHPUnit runs the engine suite without loading WordPress.

constraints.name: No frontend code before a named visual thesis and an interaction thesis; no generic AI defaults (purple gradients, three icon cards, transition: all).

modules.responsibility: justsimple/v1: six public routes (module, day and month availability, book, view and cancel by code) with per-IP rate limits and a honeypot; admin routes for modules, services, staff, shifts, qualifications, policies, hours, days off and the booking desk, behind capabilities. Phase 3 adds products (admin CRUD, public status-only list), POST /admin/bookings/{id}/items, PATCH /admin/bookings/{id} to clear schedule_conflict, and the add-on flag on services. Phase 4 adds restaurant tables, seating times and open-table rules for admins, and party size, table class, separate seating, a chosen table and minimum-spend acceptance for the public. Phase 5 adds bays, supported vehicles, parts per service and per job, and resume for admins, and the vehicle, the supported-model list and the lead-time notice for the public. Phase 6 adds service location, category and travel time, the business location, meeting rooms and links, follow-ups and actual duration for admins, and coordinates and the visit address for the public.

modules.name: Booking service
modules.responsibility: Creates bookings under a per-module GET_LOCK in one transaction, replays idempotent requests, changes statuses under row locks, sweeps expired holds before every read and from WP-Cron, keeps customers by phone without overwriting their email, and sends plain-text email through wp_mail. Salon: on-the-spot upsell under the same module lock (extend, or flag both appointments and report the clash), retail stock deducted atomically on completion, and own-appointments-only for staff linked to a WordPress user. Workshop: typed vehicles checked against supported models, the parts lead-time acknowledgement, the job parts list (row-locked), waiting for parts (time freed from now), resume under the module lock, and parts taken on completion. Field service: the on-site address with its map pin, meeting rooms on confirmation and by hand, inspection follow-ups, and overruns through the stretch-or-flag Extend shared with salon upsell.

evidence.note: Lock, decide again, defensive overlap check, insert.
